section_1.title: The Concept of Vectors vs. Scalars
section_1.content: Introduce scalars as simple magnitudes (e.g., speed) versus vectors, which carry both magnitude and direction (e.g., velocity). Use a coordinate system to define a vector as an arrow from an origin.
section_1.example: A cat running: 'Speed' is 5m/s (scalar), but 'Velocity' is 5m/s towards the food bowl (vector).

section_2.title: Visualizing Vector Components
section_2.content: Break down a 2D vector into its x (horizontal) and y (vertical) components using the Cartesian plane. Explain how any vector can be expressed as a combination of basis vectors i and j.
section_2.example: A drone flying diagonally. If it moves 3 units right and 4 units up, we represent this as the vector [3, 4].

section_3.title: Vector Addition (The Parallelogram Rule)
section_3.content: Explain how to add two vectors visually by placing the tail of one vector at the head of the other. Show the resultant vector forming the diagonal of a parallelogram.
section_3.example: A boat crossing a river: One vector is the boat's engine power, the other is the river's current. The resultant vector shows the actual path taken.

section_4.title: Scalar Multiplication and Scaling
section_4.content: Describe how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without altering its direction (unless the scalar is negative, which reverses it).
section_4.example: A laser pointer: Multiplying a vector by 2 doubles the length of the light beam, keeping it pointing at the same target on the wall.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-World Application
section_5.content: Synthesize the concepts. Conclude by highlighting how these basics are the foundation for game development, physics engines, and AI machine learning.
section_5.example: Character movement in a video game: Calculating the final position of a character by adding 'velocity' vectors over time.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars just show simple magnitude.",
            "Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.",
            "A cat's speed is a scalar.",
            "Velocity towards a bowl is a vector.",

        self.play(Create(dot))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00FFFF")
        arrow.move_to(dot.get_center())
        self.play(Transform(dot, arrow))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label = Text("Vector has magnitude and direction", font_size=20, color="#ADD8E6")
